observations: Photo 0 and photo 1 show the same teal-and-cream industrial machine from different angles, apparently a bookbinding/sewing (saddle-stitch or thread-sewing) machine with a feeder tray, multiple needle/clamp assemblies, and a control panel with push buttons.
Photo 1 shows a control box with numbered buttons, a red emergency-stop switch, and a yellow caution sticker, plus a clear plastic hopper/feeder on top.
No manufacturer nameplate, model number, or serial tag is legible in either photo.
Surfaces show grime, rust spots, and wear consistent with heavy prior use; floor and surroundings look like a workshop/factory setting.
A watermark reading 'OYOLAKFOM NIGLTD POSTED ON JIJI' appears on both images; this is a seller/platform watermark, not a brand marking on the machine.
No power cable connection, running state, or output (stitched book) is visible in either photo.

claims.evidence: No photo or clip shows the machine powered on, running, or producing output; only static shots of the idle machine are given.

risks.risk: Machine may not actually power on or complete a sewing/stitching cycle
risks.proof: A video clip of the machine running a full cycle with material feeding through

risks.risk: Missing or damaged internal parts (needles, thread guides, timing belts) not visible from outside
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the needle bar, thread path, and drive belts with covers removed

risks.risk: No visible brand/model plate, so age, original specification, and parts availability are unknown
risks.proof: A clear photo of any nameplate, serial tag, or manufacturer sticker on the frame or control box

risks.risk: Control panel electronics (buttons, emergency stop) may be faulty given visible wear
risks.proof: A clip showing the control panel lighting up and responding to button presses

risks.risk: Rust and grime suggest possible storage in damp conditions, which could affect motor and bearings
risks.proof: Photos of the motor housing and undercarriage, plus any maintenance/service records
risks.if_unproven: priced as having potential motor/bearing wear

proof_requests: Video of the machine running a full cycle (power on, feed, output)
Clear photo of any nameplate/serial number on the machine body
Close-up of the needle/thread assembly and drive belts
Photo/video of the control panel powering on and responding to inputs
Photo of the motor and undercarriage for rust/corrosion check
response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as an industrial bookbinding/sewing machine from its distinctive feeder and stitching mechanism, but the seller's 'perfect working condition' claim is unverifiable remotely with no run footage or nameplate, so it must be priced at the worst case as non-working/unbranded until proof is supplied.
